why_next: The packet's stated purpose was to end the thirteen-cycle add-at-execute/delete-at-verdict pathology and then measure amortization economics on a substrate with real cold-discovery cost. It achieved neither, and the failure is now precisely localized rather than diffuse, which is what makes one more measurement the right next move instead of a pivot. The treatment arm never reached a valid URL: I confirmed in the committed artifact that _build_action_template replaces the entire path value with the slot placeholder and that the module's own prefix-stripping helper is dead code, so every resource-B request issued an invalid path and success was 0.0 by construction of the code, not by property of inheritance. That is a fixable defect with a named location, and until it is fixed the economic question is not merely unanswered, it is unposed -- there is nothing to amortize because nothing executed. The three preregistered baselines and the incumbent reference curve did behave as expected, and the substrate's server side did impose real multi-step auth, pagination and schema-discovery work, so the substrate is reusable and the dynamic-range idea was right; it was the baseline arm that failed to actually execute that work, being a fixed 3-request policy. The durability half produced a genuinely new and precisely bounded fact: the capability is present in the tree at this commit, whereas for thirteen cycles it was not. But the promotion gate it was supposed to survive returned REVISE, and product-promote.yml requires audit PASS, so the delta reverts and the cycle repeats. That is the real finding of this packet and it is architectural rather than scientific: as long as the only sanctioned way to keep product code is to pass a gate, and no product gate has yet been shown passable on a substrate whose baselines are executed rather than simulated, the workflow will keep deleting the capability it keeps asking for. The next question is therefore built to attack the smallest unexecuted link first (can the mechanism execute a bound path at all, verified by the positive control) and only then the economics, with the baseline executed, the preregistered sample size and bootstrap restored, the full probe set run, and the null control re-judged on the criterion the preregistration actually froze. It stays in Product because only that lane's allowed_code_roots include src/ and tests/, and thirteen attempts plus the EXP-GRAPH-36118890504 audit confirm a harness substitute does not survive. It is materially different from the question just failed: the prior question assumed the mechanism worked and asked only about cost, which is why its 0.0 was ambiguous between a mechanism result and a code result.

A verified product-code defect, established by static reading of the exact committed artifact rather than by a new measurement: _build_action_template at src/spider/kernel.py lines 316-356 overwrites the entire value at a varying field path with the slot placeholder, and its two branches at lines 344-347 (the startswith('/') case and the general case) are behaviorally identical, so an induced path is '${id}' and never '/api/v1/items/${id}'.
